key_insight: Mimir shows that long-horizon irrigation control can improve when an LLM is constrained by immutable physics, numerical verification, and persistent memory of past failures rather than free-form decision making.
engineering_relevance: The work is relevant for cyber-physical control systems because it demonstrates a safe agent pattern that can act, check, and adapt over long time horizons without overriding the underlying physical model.
method: Uses a structured physical interface plus deterministic simulation to convert LLM proposals into bounded executable actions.
Repairs failures on two timescales: fast numerical revision before action and slow consolidation of recurring failure patterns into persistent context.
Keeps the simulator, evaluator, and action constraints fixed while allowing the agent’s contextual guidance to evolve.
evidence_signal: Across multiple sites, crops, and years under a common retrospective evaluator, Mimir achieved the lowest reported aggregate control cost and used about 51% less irrigation than the historical schedule replay.
watch_item: Performance depends on the fidelity of the physics model and the evaluator, so any mismatch between simulation and field conditions could limit transfer to new irrigation settings.
paper_title: Mimir: Physics-Grounded LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Irrigation Control
